findings.excerpt:
simpa only [Complex.ofReal_re, Complex.re_sum, ← Complex.ofReal_pow,
    ← Complex.ofReal_prod, Complex.mul_re, Complex.ofReal_im, mul_zero, sub_zero] using h
findings.problem: The simp set uses ← Complex.ofReal_pow and ← Complex.ofReal_prod, which run against the simp-normal direction. In Mathlib, ofReal_pow and ofReal_prod are @[simp, norm_cast] and push the coercion inward. Reversing them to fold the real powers and products back under one cast is a hand-picked orientation. It only works because of the exact shape of h, and it needs the extra rules Complex.mul_re, ofReal_im, mul_zero and sub_zero to clean up. The proof therefore depends on a bespoke simp set that fights the default normal form, and it may break if the shape of the earlier statement changes.
findings.proposed_change: Take the real part in a form that keeps the default orientation. For example, state the complex interpolation identity with the cast pushed inward (as it already is), and either use `exact_mod_cast` on `congrArg Complex.re (hc t)` after rewriting the per-term real part, or add a small local `have hterm : ∀ a, (c a * ∏ i, (v (a i) : ℂ)^(t i).val).re = (c a).re * ∏ i, v (a i)^(t i).val` proved by `rw [← Complex.ofReal_pow, ← Complex.ofReal_prod]; simp`. Then close with `simpa [hterm] using h` using the default simp set, so no reversed lemmas appear in the final call.
findings.benefit: The final step uses the standard push-cast simp normal form and a named intermediate fact. This makes the proof robust to simp-set changes and easier to read. It also avoids encouraging reversed rewrites with Complex.ofReal_pow and Complex.ofReal_prod.

findings.problem: binStateDensity is an irreducible-looking noncomputable def. Its only unfolding is the filter-card count divided by A*x. Every consumer re-opens it with `unfold` or `simp only [binStateDensity, …]` and then redoes the same conversion between the card of a filter and an indicator sum. This file does it inline in the `he` step at lines 31–34, and binStateDensity_sum unfolds it with `simp only [binStateDensity, ← sum_div, ← he]`. Other files do the same: BinMarginalInput.lean, Arithmetic/DistinctBinGenerating.lean and Arithmetic/DistinctBinDistribution.lean. There is no canonical rewrite lemma for the indicator-sum form, so each call site unfolds the whole definition and relies on a bespoke simp set.
findings.proposed_change: Add one equation lemma next to the definition (or here): `theorem binStateDensity_eq_sum_ite (J A x r) : binStateDensity J A x r = (∑ n ∈ Ioc 0 ⌊A*x⌋₊, if canonicalBinVector J x n = r then (1:ℝ) else 0)/(A*x)`. Prove it using the existing `he` argument (`sum_boole` / `← sum_filter`). Use it in binStateDensity_interpolation instead of the local `he` plus `unfold`, and in binStateGeneratingAverage_states. Do not tag it @[simp]. It is an unfolding lemma that would expand a atomic quantity at every use, so call it explicitly via `rw` or `simp only`.
findings.benefit: The unfolding is shared and named, so downstream proofs stop re-deriving the card-to-indicator conversion. They also stop depending on whether `simp only [binStateDensity]` leaves the expression in a particular shape.
